nodes.name: New Contact Form Submission
nodes.notes: Serves an n8n-hosted form (Email, Company, Dealstage). Each submission becomes one execution.

nodes.name: Normalize Contact Payload
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Normalize incoming contact records to a stable schema Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Remove Duplicate Contacts
nodes.notes: Drops duplicates within this run (compared on contactId). Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

nodes.name: Enrich — Primary Provider
nodes.notes: GET https://enrichment.example.com/v2/lookup — retries 3× with backoff on failure. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: API key / bearer for the target API. Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.

nodes.name: Primary Hit?
nodes.notes: Two-way gate on ={{ $json.company || $json.name }}. TRUE continues the happy path, FALSE takes the alternate branch. Watch out: The false branch carries the non-matching items — wire it deliberately rather than leaving it dangling.

nodes.name: Enrich — Fallback Provider
nodes.notes: GET https://fallback-enrich.example.com/v1/person — retries 3× with backoff on failure. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: API key / bearer for the target API. Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.

nodes.name: Merge Enrichment Paths
nodes.notes: Rejoins 2 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Score Enriched Records
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Score each contact 0-100 from simple heuristics Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Upsert into HubSpot
nodes.notes: Creates or updates a HubSpot contact by email — HubSpot is the CRM system of record for this pipeline. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: HubSpot private-app token. HubSpot → Settings → Integrations → Private Apps → create app → copy the token.

nodes.name: Hot Lead?
nodes.notes: Two-way gate on ={{ $json.score >= 80 }}. TRUE continues the happy path, FALSE takes the alternate branch. Watch out: The false branch carries the non-matching items — wire it deliberately rather than leaving it dangling.

nodes.name: Ping Owner Immediately
nodes.notes: Sends an email via Microsoft Outlook — recipient comes from the item's email field. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Microsoft OAuth2. Azure Portal → App registrations → Microsoft Graph → Mail.Send / Mail.Read.

nodes.name: Serialize Run Output (CSV)
nodes.notes: Serializes items to a CSV binary file.

nodes.name: Archive Row Snapshot
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Contact Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Fingerprint for Idempotency
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Build a stable idempotency key per contact (djb2 hash, no deps) Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Drop Already-Processed Items
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

nodes.name: Load Previous Snapshot
nodes.notes: Looks up an existing HubSpot contact by last-modified date — finds records the pipeline hasn't processed yet. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: HubSpot private-app token. HubSpot → Settings → Integrations → Private Apps → create app → copy the token.

nodes.name: Compute Drift vs Snapshot
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Compare current metrics with the previous snapshot Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Stamp Completion Time
nodes.notes: Stamps completedAt with the current time for auditing.

nodes.name: Persist Run Metadata
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Enrich with Reference Data
nodes.notes: GET https://enrichment.example.com/v2/lookup — retries 3× with backoff on failure. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: API key / bearer for the target API. Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.

nodes.name: Fold In Enrichment Fields
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes enrichedAt, enrichmentSource. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
nodes.notes: Delegates to a reusable sub-workflow (single-responsibility building block) and waits for its result. Watch out: The sub-workflow needs an Execute Sub-workflow Trigger as its entry point. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run.

nodes.name: Record Sub-workflow Result
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Align Field Names
nodes.notes: Normalizes field names so every source feeds the same downstream schema.

nodes.name: Guard Non-Empty email
nodes.notes: Drops items that fail the condition; only qualifying items continue (no false branch).

nodes.name: Summarize Run Stats
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes runAt, itemCount, status. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Contact Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

# Capture demo requests: HubSpot + sub-workflow

**Pattern:** Lead Capture & Routing · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Form

## Overview

Starts when the form is submitted, and covers enrichment work end to end across HubSpot, Google Sheets, Outlook and Slack.

It moves through 28 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. New Contact Form Submission
2. Normalize Contact Payload
3. Remove Duplicate Contacts
4. Enrich — Primary Provider
5. Primary Hit?
6. Enrich — Fallback Provider
7. Merge Enrichment Paths
8. Score Enriched Records
9. Upsert into HubSpot
10. Hot Lead?
11. Ping Owner Immediately
12. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
13. Archive Row Snapshot
14. Fingerprint for Idempotency
15. Drop Already-Processed Items
16. Load Previous Snapshot
17. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
18. Stamp Completion Time
19. Persist Run Metadata
20. Enrich with Reference Data
21. Fold In Enrichment Fields
22. Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
23. Record Sub-workflow Result
24. Align Field Names
25. Guard Non-Empty email
26. Summarize Run Stats
27. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
28. Send Summary to Outlook

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing enrichment work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

New Contact Form Submission → Normalize Contact Payload → Remove Duplicate Contacts → Enrich — Primary Provider → Primary Hit? → Enrich — Fallback Provider → Merge Enrichment Paths → Score Enriched Records → Upsert into HubSpot → Hot Lead? → Ping Owner Immediately → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Row Snapshot → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow → Record Sub-workflow Result → Align Field Names → Guard Non-Empty email → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Outlook → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping HubSpot and Google Sheets aligned by hand for enrichment
- Intake checked for completeness before it is stored in HubSpot, for enrichment
- Enrichment work where "Normalize Contact Payload" is still a manual step before HubSpot
- Enrichment work that only reaches HubSpot when a form is submitted, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps HubSpot and Google Sheets in step for enrichment, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in HubSpot or Google Sheets are skipped, across all 31 nodes of this enrichment build
- A failed HubSpot or Google Sheets call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 31 nodes in this enrichment build
- Branches rejoin before HubSpot, so a enrichment run reports once rather than 31 times
- Every enrichment run leaves an audit row behind, alongside HubSpot

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Google OAuth2 / service account; HubSpot private-app token; Microsoft OAuth2; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

The fallback enrichment provider only fires when the primary genuinely misses (checked explicitly, not assumed) — paying for two enrichment calls per lead when the first one already worked would double the cost for no benefit. Scoring runs after enrichment, not before, so the score reflects the richest data available rather than just what arrived on the original request.

## Practice exercises

About as deep as this pattern goes — extend it:

1. Force the primary provider to miss (e.g. a bad URL) and confirm the fallback picks up the slack.
2. Add a third-provider rung to the waterfall after the fallback.
3. Change the hot-lead threshold and watch how often the immediate-ping branch fires.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**HubSpot private-app token**
HubSpot → Settings → Integrations → Private Apps → create app → copy the token.
_Gotcha:_ Grant the CRM scopes you need; legacy API keys are deprecated and will not work.

**Microsoft OAuth2**
Azure Portal → App registrations → Microsoft Graph → Mail.Send / Mail.Read.
_Gotcha:_ Choose delegated vs application permissions deliberately; they behave differently.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your enrichment process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- HubSpot: a private-app token carrying only the CRM scopes these nodes use — legacy API keys are deprecated and over-broad.
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Outlook: use `Mail.Send` alone if nothing here reads the mailbox.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
enrichment payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
